projectMove.title: Cruise: settle your dinner time and bed setup
projectMove.body: Check-in is already done, with boarding group C02 and an 11:00 to 11:30 AM arrival on November 1, so the only open items left are your dining time and your cabin bed choice. Both live in the Carnival app, take a couple of minutes, and the better dinner slots tend to fill as sailing day gets closer, so locking them in now keeps your options open.

tip.title: Keep your boarding pass offline on your phone
tip.body: Save your Carnival boarding pass and a photo of your passport card to your phone's files so they open without signal. Port Wi-Fi and cell service can be slow on embarkation day, and having both ready offline makes the check-in line much faster.

surprise.title: Windows XP turns 25 today
surprise.body: Twenty-five years ago today, Windows XP went on sale in stores, after reaching manufacturing on August 24, 2001. The XP stood for "experience," and it brought the two-column Start menu and the Luna look that a lot of people grew up on. The famous Bliss wallpaper is a real, unedited photograph: former National Geographic photographer Charles O'Rear shot those green hills near the Napa and Sonoma county line in January 1996 on a Mamiya RZ67 with Fujifilm Velvia film, which makes it one of the most widely seen photos ever taken. Microsoft kept XP supported until April 8, 2014, more than 12 years after launch, when its products normally get about 10, and unsupported systems like it are exactly the kind of security risk the A+ material warns about.
